n: Moses climbs to the summit of Pisgah on Mount Nebo, across from Jericho, and the Lord gives him a sweeping view northward to Gilead and Dan.

f.g: A ridge or peak of the Nebo range.
The hill country east of the Jordan.
The far northern edge of Israel’s later territory.

n: His gaze moves across the central and southern lands to the Mediterranean — territories future tribes would inherit.
Then south to the Negev, the Jordan valley, Jericho the palm city, and Zoar near the Dead Sea.

f.g: Jericho, known for its palm groves.

n: God reminds Moses this is the very land promised to the patriarchs. He may see it, though not enter. Even this vision was a gift of grace.

f.w: This is the land which I sware unto Abraham
thou shalt not go over thither

n: Moses, “the servant of the Lord,” passes from mortal leadership as God said. Latter-day Saint scripture indicates the Lord took Moses to himself, and he later appeared to Jesus and to Joseph Smith.

f.w: Moses the servant of the LORD died

n: The Lord himself attended to Moses’ end, and no one knows the burial place. The JST reads that the Lord “took him unto his fathers.”

f.g: JST: “For the Lord took him unto his fathers.”

f.w: no man knoweth of his sepulchre

n: At 120 his eyesight was still clear and his strength intact. His departure was by God’s word, not weakness.
Israel mourned thirty days, the same length as for Aaron. Then the time of mourning closed and life moved forward.
Joshua was filled with wisdom because Moses had laid hands on him — an ordinance passing authority and spiritual gifts. Israel accepted his leadership.

f.w: Moses had laid his hands upon him

n: No later prophet in Israel matched Moses, who knew the Lord face to face. The “prophet like Moses” of 18:15 would be Christ himself.

f.w: whom the LORD knew face to face
there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses

n: He was unique in the signs and wonders God worked through him in Egypt.
And in the mighty, awe-inspiring deeds he performed before all Israel. So ends the five books of Moses.
